title: postgresadapter/generator.go
description: The generator for the postgres-adapter component. It emits the store, its pool and its transport policy, the baseline migration and one SQL migration with its trigger for each schema step of the declaration, so it owns that component's output contracts. Under the owner decision of 2026-11-09 the store and AutoMigrate go: ST-SUP-RC01-OC41 makes the tables from the declaration, and data access moves to the generated commands and queries.

title: postgresadapter/checkpoints.go
description: Emits the scan checkpoint migration, and renders checkpoints.go.tmpl into the load and save methods of the store checkpoint.

title: postgresadapter/cleanup.go
description: Writes the cleanup state column contract and the trigger body that records the state of each cleanup owner for a deleted row.

title: postgresadapter/cleanup_summary.go
description: Renders cleanup_summary.go.tmpl into the cleanup summary readers: one aggregate statement over pending deleted rows for a declared owner and scope.

title: postgresadapter/cleanup_targets.go
description: Writes the retained target history column, its trigger body and its migration for each declared cleanup target field.

title: postgresadapter/conditions.go
description: Writes the trigger that refuses resource conditions that are not declared or are too large, and renders conditions.go.tmpl into the version-checked condition write and the condition readers.

title: postgresadapter/cursor.go
description: Renders cursor.go.tmpl into the cursor reader of each entity: a bound ID cursor, a fixed order and one extra row.

title: postgresadapter/database.go
description: Renders database.go.tmpl into the database opener: the transport check of each connection target, the connection deadline and the pool settings.

title: postgresadapter/effects.go
description: Emits the effect binding table and its guard trigger, and renders effects.go.tmpl into the store methods that bind an effect digest in the write transaction.

title: postgresadapter/finalization.go
description: Writes the finalization column migration and the trigger body that sets the finalization time only when all cleanup owners are complete.

title: postgresadapter/go_models.go
description: Gives other generators the Go model descriptions (field names, types and pointer forms) that agree with the emitted models.go.

title: postgresadapter/related.go
description: Emits the related access and row filter methods of the store: joins only on keys of the same entity, declared columns only, bounded filters and bound values.

title: postgresadapter/resource_state.go
description: Emits the resource state table, its guard trigger and its key index migration, and renders resource_state.go.tmpl into the state load and save methods.

title: postgresadapter/resource_state_scopes.go
description: Emits the scope and key guards of the resource state table, and renders resource_state_scopes.go.tmpl into the scoped state methods.

title: postgresadapter/schema_generation.go
description: Reads the schema_generation and writer_lease settings, and renders schema_generation.go.tmpl into the write epoch and the single-writer lease code. LeaseEnabled tells other generators the lease mode. On the runtime data path (ST-SUP-RC01-OC41) it leaves out the store's identity, fence and restore methods, and keeps the bootstrap, the marker check and the ledger read.

title: postgresadapter/transaction.go
description: Renders transaction.go.tmpl into WithTransaction, WithLockedResource and Notify: queued notifications commit with the write or not at all, with the epoch and fence when they are set.

title: postgresadapter/versions.go
description: Writes the revision trigger of each versioned entity (identity that does not change, no reversed deletion, no history removal) and the current observation table, and renders versions.go.tmpl into the retained read and the version migration.

title: postgresadapter/initial_digests.go
description: Not written yet. A constant table of the known body digests of 001_initial for each postgres-adapter version, which the emitted migration code reads to keep 'A changed 001_initial body is rewritten once under guard'.

title: postgresadapter/tenant_column.go
description: The tenant column of the owned tables: the GORM tags that put the column of tenancy.key first in the primary key, in every index and in every foreign key between owned tables, the refusals of a field with the key's name and of a reference from a shared or a system entity to an owned one, and the SELECT-only access of the runtime role to a shared table.

title: postgresadapter/tables.go
description: The tables of the runtime data path (gen.Context.RuntimeData): the SQL text of 001_initial from the declaration, one CREATE TABLE for each entity with the tenant column first in a pooled service, the key id, the declared fields with their types and checks, created_time, updated_time, version and, for a protected entity, authz_token, and one unique index for each unique key with the tenant column first; the refusals of a service that needs the GORM store; and the files and wiring of that path, which emit no store and no entity model. The GORM store stays the default until the command and query generators replace it. On that path it also emits runtime_access.go: TenantConfig, the configuration of the runtime library's connectors from the adapter's opener with its verified TLS policy, loopback test mode and pool bounds, and CheckLedger, the read-only check of the migration job that refuses a database whose tables the release did not make.

title: browserbackend/generator.go
description: The generator for the browser-backend component. It checks the declaration, captures the declared assets or the captured ZIP bundle, calculates the SHA-256 hashes of the inline scripts in index.html, and selects the templates to render. It also renders the separate schema package and schema.sql, so it owns the asset policy and schema grant contracts.

title: browserbackend/backend.go.tmpl
description: The emitted backend core. It sets every session and login cookie, applies the common response headers and the content security policy, matches the declared browser routes, validates a return path, serves the captured assets, inserts the public runtime metadata and the style nonce, runs the bounded startup steps and their diagnostics, bounds telemetry admission, and checks that the console, API and identity hosts do not share a cookie host.

title: browserbackend/handlers.go.tmpl
description: The emitted HTTP handlers. They run login, the callback with its state, nonce and identity checks, the session response, the sign-out confirmation page and form, provider sign-out, the login completion document, and the API proxy. They own the origin, CSRF, bearer, proxy header and sign-out contracts.

title: browserbackend/store.go.tmpl
description: The emitted session store, together with the key reader in keys.go.tmpl. It seals each record with AES-256-GCM against the hash of the cookie ID, keeps the pending login and total record limits, claims and finishes one token renewal per session, removes a session on sign-out, and deletes expired rows. It owns the storage, renewal and key contracts.

title: browserbackend/socket.go.tmpl
description: The emitted browser socket transport. It admits a socket only for an active session with an exact origin, bounds the sockets for one session and for one backend, clears the connection deadlines after it takes over the connection, relays messages under a fixed data budget, and cancels every lease for a session that ends. It owns the socket contracts.

title: browserdom/monaco-loader.cjs
description: The emitted bundler loader for Monaco. It refuses a Monaco source file whose SHA-256 hash or replacement count is not the same as in the reviewed patch list, and it sends Monaco render operations through the STEGO DOM helpers.

title: browserdom/runtime.js
description: The emitted DOM helper module. It parses trusted render output with a fixed attribute grammar, refuses forbidden tags and output above the node and size limits, and moves style attributes into nonce style elements, so that the page policy can forbid style attributes.

title: browsertelemetry/generator.go
description: The generator for the browser-telemetry component. It resolves one service identity from the service name, the component setting and the browser backend peer setting, and it refuses two different explicit identities. It then emits three files into the output namespace: index.js with the resolved identity and the runtime source, index.d.ts with the public type declarations, and package.json with the pinned OpenTelemetry dependencies. It owns the identity and the declaration contracts of the emitted package.

title: browsertelemetry/runtime.js
description: The browser telemetry runtime that the component emits into index.js. It builds the trace, log and metric providers, the authenticated same-origin OTLP transport and the lifecycle methods. It holds every bound of the emitted package: the fixed signal paths, the session token, the export deadline, the request and response limits, the queue and batch sizes, the log, metric and attribute limits, the observable callback budgets, the public loss categories, the deployment metadata rules and the inert server-render path.

title: browseridentity/identity.go
description: Resolves the one bounded telemetry service identity from the service name and the client and backend settings, and refuses two explicit identities that are not the same. The browser telemetry and browser backend generators write this identity into the code they emit.

title: cliapplication/generator.go
description: The generator for the cli-application component. It checks the module, the output namespace and the factory package, then renders the command runtime, the configuration, output, apply, identity, session, OAuth, browser and version sources, the build identity record, the command entry point and the shared HTTPS client. The entry point it emits owns one telemetry runtime for each invocation and maps the command result to a fixed outcome.

title: cliapplication/runtime.go.tmpl
description: The command runtime that the component emits. It checks the application's definitions before any configuration read or request, parses and bounds the arguments and the request body, binds path parameters, reserves the output destination, sends one bounded HTTPS request and applies the response contract for JSON, empty and failed answers. It also converts a relative duration flag to one absolute UTC timestamp.

title: cliapplication/oauth.go.tmpl
description: The OIDC runtime that the component emits. It discovers the provider over bounded HTTPS clients, holds the restricted verification profile for ID tokens, performs the browser and device grants with S256 proof and accepts a token answer only after the issuer, audience, time, authorized party, nonce and token hash checks pass. It also keeps a refreshed session identity equal to the original identity.

title: cliapplication/config.go.tmpl
description: The configuration store that the component emits. It finds the configuration file, opens its parent directory as a root and refuses a directory that permits writes by other users. It writes the configuration with mode 0600 through an exclusive temporary file, a file sync, an atomic rename and a directory sync. It refuses an existing configuration file that permits group or other access. It keeps only an absolute reference to the token file and reads that file on demand. Logout attempts provider revocation, removes the local configuration even when revocation fails, keeps the external token file and reports the revocation error. It also bounds each input file and refuses a file that is not regular.

title: cliapplication/output.go.tmpl
description: The output destination that the component emits. It reserves the selected output file before the command reads credentials or sends its request. It opens the parent directory as a root and refuses a directory that permits writes by other users. It creates the file with exclusive creation and mode 0600, so it refuses an existing file, a symbolic link and a device. It returns the error and sends no file output to stdout after a file failure. It syncs the file and the directory after a write, keeps the file when a write fails, and removes an unwritten reservation at close.

title: cliapplication/identity.go.tmpl
description: The identity command that the component emits. It builds its report only from the fields of a successful API response and from the configured API address. It puts no locally decoded claim, no access token and no other response field into that report. It requires the output file option before it shows a raw or a decoded token. It refuses the raw and the decoded options together. It reserves the output file before it reads credentials, so a failed identity request or a failed decoding leaves no output file.

title: cliapplication/session.go.tmpl
description: The session guard that the component emits. It holds a persistent lock file on the configuration and waits for it, so concurrent processes refresh a token once. It reads the external token file through the configuration on each request. It saves the pending refresh state before it sends the token request, while it holds the lock. It refuses a session with a pending refresh and asks for a new login, so it never uses the old refresh token again. It also revokes a session at the provider.

title: cliapplication/apply.go.tmpl
description: The apply command that the component emits. It checks every document and resolves every target before it starts a resource write. It stops before any write after a lookup failure, a malformed or ambiguous list answer or a missing required create field. A dry run reports the validated status and returns before it reads credentials, refreshes a session or contacts the API. It reports one status for each document, reports the unknown status for an uncertain write and writes each resource once. Its results hold only the kind, the name, the identifier and the status, so they hold no spec value and no API error body. It gives an immutable resource the unchanged status and sends it no PATCH and no DELETE.

title: cliapplication/apply_input.go.tmpl
description: The apply input reader that the component emits. It accepts only the JSON subset of YAML. It walks each YAML node and refuses an anchor, an alias, a merge key, a custom tag and a duplicate key. It refuses invalid Unicode, a NUL byte and a number that is not valid JSON. It keeps each number as an exact JSON number, so a large integer stays exact. It bounds the document count, the byte count, the node count and the depth. It inspects each named file with a link check and opens it without link following, so it refuses a symbolic link, a FIFO, a device and a file that is not regular.

title: cliapplication/apply_immutable.go.tmpl
description: The immutable apply support that the component emits. It requires that an immutable identity names unique required string create fields, and it refuses a definition that also declares patch fields. It builds the lookup search from the exact values of those fields, so it finds the resource by exact identity. It compares the stored row with the requested fields and reports a difference as an error. It also refuses a malformed or an ambiguous list answer before any write.

title: controller/generator.go
description: The generator for the controller component. It emits the watch runtime, the keyed scheduler, the cursor scanner, the sweep runtime, the state codec and journal, the metrics monitor and the process entry point, so it owns that component's output contracts. The runtime, keyed, scan, sweep, process and state templates hold the session rules, the scheduling rules, the page rules and the privacy rules.

title: gosdk/generator.go
description: The generator for the go-sdk component. It loads the captured OpenAPI document and its declared references, bounds the input, runs the pinned wire generator with the nullable type option, renders the shared bounded HTTPS transport, and emits the public typed client package.

title: gosdk/client.go.tmpl
description: The source of the emitted public SDK client. It checks the bearer token, builds the bounded HTTPS transport, keeps the request bridge private, bounds the active calls, and bounds the wait in Close.

title: gosdk/input.go
description: Gives the compiler the OpenAPI input files that the Go SDK declaration names, and loads the OpenAPI document that the generator renders the client from.

title: grpcapplication/generator.go
description: The generator for the grpc-application component. It compiles the declared protobuf contracts, renders the runtime, the client, the stream header helper and the timestamp conversion, and serves each declared method through the generated handler of the command or query whose Method names it. It binds no registration factory (ST-SUP-RC07-OC18). On the runtime data path ValidateContext and Generate go to runtime_data.go (ST-SUP-RC07-OC19); the GORM store path keeps the factory until the store path is removed.

title: grpcapplication/runtime.go.tmpl
description: The source of the emitted gRPC runtime: its TLS configuration, the verifier interceptors, the admission and message limits, the unary deadline, the stream lifetime and input and output timeouts, the error and panic isolation, the registered cleanup list and the prepared registrar.

title: grpcapplication/client.go.tmpl
description: The source of the emitted outbound gRPC client: its fixed credentials and server identity check, its per-call private token read, its call and stream limits, and the bounded stream wrapper that completes client telemetry on every terminal path.

title: grpcapplication/stream_headers.go.tmpl
description: The source of the emitted stream header helper. It checks each declared header requirement for name shape, value shape, duplication and count before it reads a stream, and reports a contract error without touching the stream.

title: grpcapplication/conversion.go.tmpl
description: The source of the emitted checked timestamp conversion, shared by the grpc-application and grpc-processes components. It bounds the protobuf instant range, keeps optional presence, owns each result and drops the monotonic clock and the local zone.

title: grpcapplication/mapping.go
description: The response mapping emitter of the gRPC generators. It matches the declared provider model fields and prepared inputs to the compiled protobuf message, and emits pure conversion functions with their presence, ownership, numeric, timestamp and JSON bounds.

title: grpcapplication/grpcgen/export.go
description: Exports GenerateFile, which runs the pinned copy of protoc-gen-go-grpc 1.6.1 with its default options (unimplemented server required, generic streams).

title: grpcapplication/grpcgen/grpc.go
description: A vendored copy of the upstream protoc-gen-go-grpc code generator (Apache-2.0). It emits the _grpc.pb.go service, client and server descriptors for each declared proto service.

title: grpcapplication/overlay.go
description: Makes sure that each declared proto source that pins a frozen reference contract extends it conservatively, with no changed or reused field numbers. It emits a test file that pins the checked descriptor next to the generated protobuf code.

title: grpcapplication/proto.go
description: Reads the declared proto sources as compiler inputs, compiles them, checks the overlays, and emits the protobuf Go code and the gRPC service code through grpcgen. generator.go (RC07) and standalone.go (RC08) call it. Methods gives the kind of each method of the services of the proto files, which the compiler reads for the check of ST-DECL-INV73 and the stream queries (ST-SUP-RC33-OC08); compileSources compiles the files for both.

title: grpcapplication/runtime_data.go
description: The runtime data path of the grpc-application component (gen.Context.RuntimeData). It takes the setting proto_files alone and refuses factory_package, naming ST-DECL-INV72, and every other setting. It compiles the proto files; a file of the command component's proto_files keeps the Go package of the command contract and gets no Go code here, so a command's request and response are one Go type over HTTP and gRPC (ST-SUP-RC32-OC11). It binds each method that a declared command or query names: a command to its handler command handlers <Command>RPC on command.ServeRPC, after it checks that the method takes the command's request and response messages; a get query to queries/serve Serve<Query>RPC with the getter of the resource member's string field; a list query to Serve<Query>RPC with the getters of the fields cursor and limit, and a response with the fields items and next; a stream query to Serve<Query>Stream (ST-SUP-RC33-OC08). It emits the Go code and the service stubs of the other proto files, the transport runtime, and server.go: one server type for each service with a declared method, which embeds the Unimplemented server, so a method that no declaration names answers Unimplemented; and NewRuntime, which makes the handlers on the runtimes of the running service, the transport runtime that verifies each bearer token with the verifier of the service, and serves only in the api mode. The wiring of main.go is one constructor that takes the runtime wiring of the service and runs as a background task. It imports no package of the service's author (ST-SUP-RC07-OC18).

title: grpcapplication/standalone.go
description: The grpc-processes generator. It accepts only the process and protobuf settings, requires a JWT verifier and telemetry, refuses a storage contract or a primary API factory, and emits the compiled contracts, the shared transport and one executable for each declared process. From 2.0.0 it binds no factory: it emits the process method slot and one handler for each declared process method (ST-SUP-RC08-OC09 to ST-SUP-RC08-OC12).

title: grpcapplication/process.go
description: The process runtime emitter shared by the grpc-application and grpc-processes components. It checks the domain Open declaration, renders the process package and renders one main program for each declared process, with its initialization, supervision, failure isolation and shutdown bounds.

title: grpcapplication/process_health.go.tmpl
description: The source of the emitted process health monitor and probe command. It validates the monitor address, serves only the liveness and readiness paths from the process state, and runs a bounded probe that does no domain work.

title: healthcheck/generator.go
description: The generator for the health-check component. It emits the sampling monitor, the liveness and readiness handlers and the optional application monitor, and it registers both probe routes on the top-level mux, so it owns that component's output contracts.

title: httpapplication/generator.go
description: The generator for the http-application component. It renders the transport package, the HTTPS client, the field projector and the response mapping package, and it mounts the routes of the declared commands, queries and collections on the generated runtime that owns the database, the server limits, signal handling and request draining. It binds no application factory (ST-SUP-RC10-OC35).

title: httpclient/client.go.tmpl
description: The source of the bounded HTTPS client that this component emits into the application's client package. It fixes verified TLS 1.3, one origin, the request and response limits, the request permit count, the stream limits, the private credential file rule and the optional certificate pin. Other components render the same template, so the contracts it keeps are shared.

title: httpapplication/endpoint.go.tmpl
description: The source of the emitted transport package: the endpoint and reply endpoint builders, the strict JSON body reader, the order parser and the response limits. It owns the request lifecycle contracts of the component.

title: httpapplication/fields.go.tmpl
description: The source of the emitted bounded list projector: the field schema, its copy and bounds, the selector parser, the list projection and the optional projection adapter.

title: httpapplication/responses.go
description: The response mapping emitter of the http-application component. It reads the captured OpenAPI object and the provider's Go model, checks that each declared property has one rule, and emits pure conversion functions with their encoding, numeric, timestamp, enum and JSON bounds.

title: httpapplication/response_inputs.go
description: Reads the declared prepared response inputs and binds a response field to one input. It refuses a field that names an input and also a model source or a constant. It prepares the response mapping that responses.go emits.

title: httpapplication/diagnostic_probe.go
description: Not written yet. Version 2.0.0 of the http-application component: the HTTP server reports its diagnostics as the built-in event http.server.diagnostic of the probe runtime, so it owns 'A server diagnostic goes through the probe runtime'. Until it is written, the fallback logger of 1.14.0 writes to standard error.

title: jwtauth/generator.go
description: The generator for the jwt-auth component. It emits the verifier, the HTTP middleware, the JWKS key set, the remote key source, the key telemetry hook and the grant policy, so it owns that component's output contracts. It also validates the header, the mode and the role claim path before it generates.

title: kafkaproducer/generator.go
description: The generator for the kafka-producer component. It emits the single-topic publisher and the runtime that joins the publisher to the outbox worker, so it owns that component's output contracts. The publisher template holds the transport rules, the credential-file rules, the acknowledgement policy and the uncertain-result policy.

title: keycloakprovider/generator.go
description: The generator for the keycloak-provider component. It emits the realm-bound administrator client, the checked native, browser and service-account lifecycles, the role, scope and mapper operations, and the service-account token proof, so it owns that component's output contracts. It requires the generated HTTP application client and a shared JWT verifier peer.

title: keycloakprovider/managed.go
description: Reads the managed_clients component settings and generates the identity and binding helpers for each declared kind. It gives every ownership attribute the reserved stego.owner. prefix and builds the legacy rename map, so it owns the component's ownership binding contract.

title: kubernetesclient/generator.go
description: The generator validates its context and then emits exactly ten Go files into the component's output namespace. It requires a Go-safe output namespace and a bound `application-http` peer, and it fails when the generated HTTP client is absent. It parses each embedded template with the output package name and the peer transport import path, formats the result, and checks that every file belongs to the declared namespace. The withdrawn pinned admission prototype is not in that list, so it cannot reach a generated project.

title: kubernetesclient/client.go.tmpl
description: This template emits the core resource client. It reads the private token file for each request, forces `fieldValidation=Strict` on writes, and rejects a malformed write path or query before any I/O. It decodes responses with exact JSON numbers and refuses anything that is not one JSON object. `Ensure`, `PatchOwned` and `DeleteOwned` require the caller's ownership labels, the observed UID and the observed resource version, never retry a conflict, and never change the caller's objects. `APIError` and `FailureSummary` expose only the method, the status and the retry delay.

title: kubernetesclient/observe.go.tmpl
description: This record covers the package observation templates: observe.go.tmpl, discovery.go.tmpl, watch_set.go.tmpl, readiness.go.tmpl and route.go.tmpl. They emit the bounded list and watch with its reset and replace discipline, the uncached API requirement check, the assigned namespace watch sets with their aggregate limits, the Deployment availability check, and the passthrough Route admission with its probe order. They make no network call of their own for an observation check.

title: kubernetesclient/tls_secret.go.tmpl
description: This record covers the package Secret and credential templates: tls_secret.go.tmpl, secret_set.go.tmpl, secret_state.go.tmpl and image_pull_secret.go.tmpl. They emit the TLS Secret and client certificate verifiers with their explicit trust pool, the trust bundle parser, the Secret set with its data digest and its validate-before-write order, the durable Secret state helper, and the image pull credential operation with its namespace identity checks. Their errors carry no Secret or credential data.

title: kubernetesservice/generator.go
description: Validates the deployment declaration and assembles the service manifest template. It builds the restricted Pod with a non-root security context, the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile, a read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation and all capabilities dropped. It sets the HTTPS probes on /livez and /readyz, the explicit TLS environment, the ClusterIP Service and the NetworkPolicy. The policy declares both policy types, adds the DNS rule, and refuses an ingress peer for a port the workload does not expose. Unbound external endpoints stay as a CIDR value that Kubernetes refuses.

title: kubernetesservice/render.go.tmpl
description: The renderer that the component emits with each project. It checks the image digest, the namespace and the file group before it renders. It expands each external endpoint binding into one host prefix and one TCP port, and refuses a missing, unknown, repeated or out-of-scope binding. It adds image pull Secret references, selects an existing account, sets the configuration digest annotation, splits the cluster and namespace scopes by known resource kind, and applies owner labels without replacing a generated label.

title: kubernetesservice/allocation_policy.go
description: Emits the allocator ClusterRole, its binding and the ValidatingAdmissionPolicies with their bindings, and so implements Admission policies fail closed, The allocator cannot change its own controls, The allocator has no Secret access, Narrow NetworkPolicy permissions and Deny-all allocation policy shape. Today the file sits in internal/generator/kubernetesservice; it moves to internal/generator/namespaceallocation with the component, and the kubernetes-service base then carries none of it (ST-SUP-RC15-OC38).

title: kubernetesservice/allocation_pods.go
description: Emits the Pod admission policy of each profile, and so implements Pod policy covers status and ephemeral writes, Allocated Pod account and token rule, An absent runtime class makes no claim, Application Pod rules only add denials and Network output keys need the node identity. Today the file sits in internal/generator/kubernetesservice; it moves to internal/generator/namespaceallocation with the component, and the kubernetes-service base then carries none of it (ST-SUP-RC15-OC38).

title: kubernetesservice/workers.go
description: Validates worker declarations and writes their image files, entry point and manifest template. The Containerfile builds with CGO disabled from a digest-pinned builder image into a scratch runtime stage with user 65532:65532 and an explicit entry point. The ignore file excludes the whole context, then permits the module files and the declared source directories, and excludes hidden files and private-key extensions. Each worker manifest contains an account, a network policy and a Deployment with one replica and the Recreate strategy, and no Service, container port or ingress rule.

title: kubernetesservice/rpc.go
description: Validates each RPC process declaration and writes its image files and manifest template. It resolves the peer component and the one declared process, and it checks the factory source directory. It gives the Deployment one replica, and it uses RollingUpdate with one extra Pod and zero unavailable Pods unless the declaration selects Recreate. It sets the gRPC listener to port 9090 with the certificate and the key files from the mounted file Secret, and it sets the monitor address to a loopback address. It exposes only the container port 9090 and gives the Service exactly that one port. Its startup, readiness and liveness probes run the process entry point with a probe mode.

title: kubernetesservice/allocation_control_accounts.go
description: Emits the control-account guard and the installer ClusterRole that is never bound, and so implements The control account installer is never bound. Today the file sits in internal/generator/kubernetesservice; it moves to internal/generator/namespaceallocation with the component, and the kubernetes-service base then carries none of it (ST-SUP-RC15-OC38).

title: kubernetesservice/local_application.go
description: Adds the local application container to the browser Pod. The container listens on a loopback address and reads its settings from its own environment Secret. It receives its own file Secret volume and its own temporary volume, and it shares no volume with the browser container. It declares no container port, so the Pod exposes it to no other Pod. It drops all capabilities, refuses privilege escalation and uses a read-only root file system. It receives no OAuth, session, database or public TLS material and no service account token.

title: kubernetesservice/external.go
description: Reads the required and optional external endpoint names, and refuses names that are not distinct DNS labels and more than 32 names. The renderer and the NetworkPolicy use these names.

title: kubernetesservice/identity.go
description: Reads kubernetes_api and kubernetes_permissions, refuses permissions without the API or above the limit, emits the Role or ClusterRole and its binding, and adds the projected token and CA volume to the Pod only when the API is selected.

title: kubernetesservice/worker_input.go
description: Gives the compiler the worker.go source file of each declared worker package as an input, and makes sure that each source is a valid Go package that can be imported and that has the worker function.

title: kubernetesworkload/workload.go.tmpl
description: The construction library that the component emits with each project. Build checks the declaration, then returns a Deployment and an optional ClusterIP Service. It fixes non-root execution, the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile, a read-only root filesystem, denied privilege escalation and the removal of all Linux capabilities. It permits only Secret, ConfigMap and bounded emptyDir volumes, mounts the first two read-only, and gives a Secret file mode 0440. It requires a digest-pinned image, three HTTP probes for each container against that container's own ports, positive requests within the limits, and exactly the dependencies that the mounts and Secret environment references name. It sets the configuration digest annotation on the Pod template and keeps dependency contents out of the result. Fields that this profile owns use explicit null values when the declaration omits them.

title: oteltracing/generator.go
description: The generator for the otel-tracing component. It emits the telemetry runtime, its validated export settings, the trace, log and metric providers, the HTTP, client, database, controller, startup and outbox signal helpers and the auth key refresh hook, so it owns that component's output contracts.

title: oteltracing/service_probe.go
description: Not written yet. Version 1.20.0 of the otel-tracing component: the runtime sends its service events as built-in observations through the probe runtime and writes nothing of its own to standard error, so it owns 'Service events go through the probe runtime' and 'No sanctioned signal goes to standard error'. Until it is written, the runtime of 1.19.0 writes its local JSON service events to standard error. This state must not be released: 1.20.0 is released only with this code, and it must meet the quality bar again at its digest (ST-SUP-INV07).

title: outbox/generator.go
description: The generator for the outbox component. On the runtime data path (gen.Context.RuntimeData) it emits only internal/outbox/outbox.go on github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime/outbox (ST-SUP-RC18-OC30): the destinations of the service with their payload limits (audit-sink when the service has the audit-log component), the migration that runs outbox.Migration of the pinned runtime with the runtime role and the worker role after a step that replaces the queue table of the former component, the queue and the worker with each destination registered, and no grant. On the store path it emits the PostgreSQL queue, its SQL migration, the delivery worker and the live event source that the GORM store, kafka-producer and the gRPC watch call, until generated CRUD runs on the runtime (ST-SUP-RC20-OC37); the queue, worker and source templates hold the transaction rules, the lease rules and the notice rules. The runtime path is in runtime.go.

title: postgresclient/generator.go
description: The generator for the postgres-client component. It emits the explicit read operation, the logical database lifecycle, the schema callback and the credential helpers, so it owns that component's output contracts. The client, provision, schema and credential templates hold the transport rules, the session rules, the ownership rules and the telemetry rules.

title: restapi/generator.go
description: The generator for the rest-api component. It emits one handler per collection, the router and its storage interface, the RFC 9457 problem type and its constructors, the OpenAPI document, the request validation middleware, the CORS middleware and the discovery handler. When the idempotency component is in the service, the OpenAPI document carries the Idempotency-Key header and its 400, 409 and 422 problem responses on each create and patch operation (ST-SUP-RC30-OC01). It therefore owns every output contract of the component except the route patterns. On the runtime data path (gen.Context.RuntimeData), which the compiler does not switch on yet, the helper runtime_data.go emits instead of the store handlers: the data package with the entity declarations of the command runtime (command.EntityFile of ST-SUP-RC32) and the read-only values of the query runtime (query.ViewFile of ST-SUP-RC33); runtime.go with the Runtime of the handlers, the handler steps around Run of the command generator (command.RunHelpers) and the answers of the errors of Run; and one handler per collection whose create, update, patch and delete each run one generated command through command.Run and whose read and list each run one query through query.Run (ST-SUP-RC20-OC37). The bound before and validate slots run in the command's fill before its write, and a refusal rolls the command back and writes the denied audit row; a halt writes nothing and marks its stored response, so no after slot runs for it or its replay; the after slots run after the command committed and wrote, and not after a replay, and a failed after slot is logged with no error text and the committed response is answered, until the after slots run through the outbox, as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-RC20-OC34). A row that is not there is 403 for an operation that decides a permission, as a deny is, until the handler answers both 404 (ST-SUP-RC29-OC02), as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11. The router then declares no storage interface, and the wiring gives each collection one constructor, New<Collection>Handler(service.CollectionRuntime()) with the operators of its bound slots, and one literal route per operation; service is the runtime wiring that the compiler writes into main.go. The path refuses an update, a patch or a delete with no permission or a public one, upsert, a scope of more than one field or level, a scope field that is not a required ref or that a patch may change, an implicit field that is not text or enum, a path parameter that is not the scope field, a field of type bytes, a slot it does not call, and a create that is not public, until the runtime decides a top-level create on the service-level resource (ST-SUP-RP10-LC31), as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11; a PUT and a DELETE, and a create or a patch without the header when it is not required, run with a key of the request's own until command.Run runs a command with an empty key without the idempotency wrapper (ST-SUP-RP10-LC11), as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11; a list pages by the sealed cursor of the query runtime and orders by declared fields with the key last (ST-SUP-RC20-OC38), as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11. Since the runtime update of 2026-11-11: a list on the runtime data path reads orderBy (declared fields that are not secret, each asc or desc) and orders by created_time descending when it names none, with the key last in the query runtime (ST-SUP-RC20-OC38, ST-SUP-RP11-LC18); a deny of a write is 404, as a missing row; the emitted NewID and ValidUUID are the runtime's; a top-level create that is not public is refused until the declaration can name the service-level resource of the tenant provisioning (ST-SUP-RC29-OC01, ST-DECL-UC10). On the runtime data path each bound after slot is staged in the command's transaction on the outbox destination rest-api.after-slots, with the slot request as JSON, and AfterSlots runs it in the outbox worker, retries a failure and counts each failure and each retry in a metric and a log line that name the slot and hold no error text (ST-SUP-RC20-OC34); the handlers bind and answer through the command runtime's BindIdentity, OutcomeOf and RecordFailure (ST-SUP-RP10-LC34). On the runtime data path a jsonb field is served: the API type holds it as json.RawMessage, a pointer to one when it is optional, and the row type of the command runtime as []byte, so the handler of an entity with a jsonb field converts the two field by field (<collection>ToData and <collection>FromData), and an optional jsonb field that is not set is NULL and absent from the answer. On the runtime data path a scoped collection takes its parent from the path parameter of its scope field: a create forces the scope field, a read, update, patch or delete of a row of another parent is not found, and a list filters on it; an implicit field is forced on a write and filtered on a list and a read; a list takes the search parameter through query.ParseSearch on the fields that are not secret, ref, jsonb or implicit; and each write that sets a ref to an entity with a resource type loads that row, on which the command runtime decides the reference (ST-SUP-RC20-OC23, ST-SUP-RC20-OC24, ST-SUP-RP11-LC20). On the runtime data path an upsert is one generated command: it finds the row of the natural key with the list of command.KeyListRead, creates a new row as a create does, decided on the rows it refers to, or locks the stored row, decides the upsert permission on it and updates it as an update does, and answers 201 or 200; it refuses an upsert with no key, with optimistic concurrency (ST-SUP-Q105), with no permission on a stored row, or whose insert decides nothing. Each handler imports the command runtime, which binds the identity.

title: restapi/http_routes.go
description: The route table of the rest-api component. It maps each collection operation to one HTTP method and path, adds the three unauthenticated discovery routes, checks each path and each parameter name, and declares the patterns to the compiler before rendering. It owns the base-path and route-shape contracts.

title: rhssoauth/generator.go
description: The generator for the rh-sso-auth component. It calls the jwt-auth generator for the shared verifier and key source, then emits the SSO handler with its exact public paths and the SSO claim mapping, so it owns that component's output contracts. title: rhssoauth/runtime_auth.go
description: RuntimeAuth of rh-sso-auth: on the runtime data path rh-sso-auth is a configuration of oidc-auth (oidcauth.Configure) with the Red Hat SSO issuer form https://<host>/auth/realms/<realm>, the subject claim sub, the tenant claim org_id and the algorithm RS256, and no verifier of its own. It refuses a key file or a key URL other than the default, because the key set comes from the discovery document of the issuer, and public paths other than the defaults, because the probes of the runtime data path answer outside the verifier. The compiler refuses a declaration whose tenancy claim is not org_id.

title: runtimeconfig/generator.go
description: The generator for the runtime-configuration component. It emits one typed settings struct, one loader and one explicit reader for each declared group, so it owns that component's output contracts. The configuration template holds the lookup rules, the default rules, the type rules, the error rules and the redaction rules.

title: tslsearch/generator.go
description: The generator for the tsl-search component. It emits the search engine and the field map for the declared entities, so it owns that component's output contracts. The search template holds the input limits, the field checks, the parameter binding and the SQL conversion.

title: typescriptsdk/generator.go

It loads the captured OpenAPI document and its declared references through the shared bounded loader, refuses the unsupported schema features, bounds the declared public error codes, and emits the ES module, the separate request and response model declarations and the package metadata.

title: typescriptsdk/runtime.js
description: The browser transport this component emits. It fixes the HTTPS browser origin, the same-origin fetch settings, the session CSRF exchange before a mutation, the input and response checks, the size, time and concurrency bounds, the private error shape, the login and logout routes and the per-operation trace context.

title: typescriptsdk/session.go

title: cipipeline/generator.go
description: Not written yet. The generator for the ci-pipeline component: it emits the provider's CI file with the pinned shared pipeline, the trusted signer, the separate build and signing jobs and the delivery policy file the platform's gate enforces, so it owns every contract of the component.

title: kubernetesservice/allocation.go.tmpl
description: The allocator package emitted into the service as deploy/allocation: Ensure, Delete, RequireNamespace, NamespaceUID and NamespaceGone. title: kubernetesservice/allocation.go
description: Reads allocation_roles, allocation_profiles and the allocator worker from the declaration, refuses what is out of bounds, and renders the allocator. title: kubernetesservice/allocation_network_metadata.go

title: kubernetesservice/allocation_pod_rules.go

title: kubernetesservice/allocation_service_accounts.go

title: tenancy/generator.go
description: The generator for the tenancy component: its checks and the row-level security migration of the owned tables, which the PostgreSQL adapter registers in its migration ledger, and the role migration. The tenant column and its keys are the PostgreSQL adapter's (ST-SUP-RC01-OC40), the grants of the runtime role come from the database access contract, and the transaction of each read and write is the command and query runtime's (ST-SUP-RP10-LC30). The Tenant type, the context accessor, the set_config transaction helper and the claim extractor live in the runtime library. The role migration also makes the worker role and the relay role, named from the runtime role with _worker and _relay, gives the owner role membership in stego_outbox_relay WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT TRUE and gives that role CREATE on public (ST-SUP-RC27-OC04); the package exports WorkerRole and RelayRole, which the runtime wiring reads.

title: tenancy/iteration.go
description: Not written yet: it waits for the runtime pin (ST-SUP-INV10, ST-GEN-INV13). The per-tenant iteration of the emitted workers and controllers through tenant.EachListed.

title: tenancy/isolation.go
description: Not written yet. The isolation test suite that the component emits, which runs as the runtime role.

title: tenancy/provisioning.go
description: Not written yet: it waits for the runtime pin and the command, authorization and audit generators. Provision and Retire, their audit rows and the tenant check of each request. The migration job of the service runtime makes the tenant list (ST-SUP-Q97).

title: auditlog/generator.go
description: The generator for the audit-log component. From the audit setting (ST-DECL-EN10), the port bindings, the field sensitivities of the entities and the settings of the component (anchor_period, retention_months) that the compiler gives it in gen.Context, it emits the package internal/auditlog on the pinned runtime library: the audit settings, the sensitive fields of each entity and which entities hold a pii field, the migration that runs the DDL text of the runtime with the runtime role, the anchor period and the retention, and the jobs of controller mode at the anchor period; and it gives the database grants, SELECT and INSERT only on audit_event. It refuses a declaration that turns audit off or does not bind the audit sink port. Not written yet: the audit write in each mutation, the denied-path write and the read audit (they wait on the command and query generators, ST-SUP-RC32 and ST-SUP-RC33), the writer and the outbox binding to the audit sink (they wait on ST-SUP-RP05-LC14), the registration of the jobs (it waits on ST-SUP-RP09-LC13), and the entity history query. The audit.Event type, the hash chain, the canonical encoder, the differ, the redaction, the partition job, the anchor publisher and the verifier live in the runtime library. Under the decision of 2026-11-09 the example services use this component and no longer declare their own AuditEvent entity.

title: spicedbauthz/generator.go
description: The generator for the spicedb-authz component. From the authorization setting (ST-DECL-EN11), the captured schema, the entities, the collections, the slot bindings, the pooled tenancy and the settings of the component (alert_bound, watch_interval) that the compiler gives it in gen.Context, it emits the package internal/authz on the pinned runtime library: the schema with the floor marker definition stego_floor added (Schema and schema.zed), the operation-to-permission table, the tenant-qualified resource of each protected entity through the runtime's NewResource, the tuples and the tuple writes of each entity's relationships through the handle, the relations of each slot binding, the migration that adds authz_token, runs the runtime's Migration and grants the worker role UPDATE on authz_token only, the runtime constructor, the relay with the owning tables and the alert bound, its start-up check and its registration on the outbox worker, and the late-revocation watch, and WriteSchema, which the migration job runs to write the schema to SpiceDB before the service starts (ST-SUP-RC29-OC23). It refuses, before any file, a declaration that the authorization checks of Declaring refuse and a service without pooled tenancy on tenant_id. Not written yet: the Evaluate calls, the list filter, the router and the revocation status route, the slot adapter and the conformance tests, which wait on the command and query generators (ST-SUP-RC32, ST-SUP-RC33); and the wiring of the relay and the watch in the service's main. The two port interfaces, the provider, the consistency mapping, the relay, the revocation records and the token codec live in the runtime library.

title: idempotency/generator.go
description: The generator for the idempotency component. From the declaration's idempotency setting, it emits the key table schema as the runtime's idempotency.Migration, the settings (the retention, with 24h as the default, the fingerprint, the problem type URIs under the problem base, and each create and patch operation of each collection that takes the Idempotency-Key header, required or accepted), one fingerprint function for each such operation over the body fields the operation declares, and the purge job, which it registers as a background task with the process database. The rest-api component writes the header and its problem responses into the OpenAPI document. A collection create or patch is a generated command (ST-SUP-RC20-OC37), so the wrapper is the one that command.Run calls. Not written yet: the use of the settings and the fingerprint functions by the generated commands, which comes with ST-SUP-RC20-OC37, and the conformance tests. The transaction wrapper, the canonical JSON fingerprint and Purge live in the runtime library.

title: ledger/generator.go
description: Not written yet. The generator for the ledger component. It emits the migration that applies the runtime ledger's DDL text with the declared codes and account limits as CHECK constraints, the REST endpoints, the ledger port that posts through the runtime ledger, the snapshot, check and expiry sweep job registrations and the OpenAPI schema, so it owns every contract of the component. It emits no posting SQL (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05).

title: command/generator.go
description: The generator for the command component. From the declared commands that the compiler gives it in gen.Context (each with the slot its fill implements), the entities, the authorization and the tenancy, and the proto files of its setting proto_files, it emits for each command: the command slot contract in the package commands, which the fill imports (the fill type that takes the decoded request message and one command handle only, the command handle, the typed refusals and the repository declarations of the written entities with Scan, Values, State, KeyChanged, Clone, ValidID and Parent, the one entity with a resource type that a row refers to, also for an entity with a resource type of its own; two such references or an optional one are refused); the Go code of the request and response messages <Command>Request and <Command>Response, written with protoc-gen-go from the compiled proto files (ST-SUP-RC32-OC11); the command declaration with its writes, destinations, relations, retry on conflict, lock timeout, typed probe of the domain-probe component, permission and resource with its FOR SHARE token statement (ST-SUP-RP10-LC31); one HTTP and one gRPC handler that bind the verified tenant and principal, require the idempotency key, run the one fill through Run and answer a deny with 403 (404 from the decision of 2026-11-11, ST-SUP-RC32-OC06), a declared refusal with its status and code, a conflict with 409 conflict or ABORTED and any other error with 500 internal, with the audit row of a denied or failed command in its own short transaction; and the binding of each command to its fill folder. It refuses, naming the command and the fill, a fill that does not implement command.command, and every declaration that the runtime would refuse at start. The helper files hold the entity declarations (entities.go), the message compilation (messages.go), the names (names.go), the rendering of the packages (render.go) and the serve helpers (serve.go), which the runtime has no command HTTP helper for yet; the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that they move to command.Serve and command.ServeRPC (ST-SUP-RP10-LC33). The check of each command fill's import closure (ST-SUP-RC32-OC03) runs in internal/fill/closure.go, a helper of the import rule fill.checkImports (ST-EXT-INV05-RL), behind the compiler's FillQualifier port, because a generator does no file or process access: fill.QualificationFaults runs go list -e -deps on each command fill, without test files, in the service module with no workspace and a read-only module graph, and gives one fault fill-imports for each refused package with the fill, its place commands[i].fill and the import chain. The outcome audit row is written on a context that the request's cancel does not end, with a short time limit. The gRPC handler gives Run the deterministic binary form of the message and fingerprints its canonical JSON form. Every destination is given as must land and idempotent until the destinations setting declares both and CommandSpec takes the effect names, as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-RC32-OC12). Since the runtime update of 2026-11-11: the handlers package holds one command.ServeSpec per command, served by command.Serve and command.ServeRPC (ST-SUP-RP10-LC33), and serve.go with RunHelpers is gone since generated CRUD calls the runtime's BindIdentity, OutcomeOf and RecordFailure (ST-SUP-RP10-LC34); the contract helpers (NewID, ValidUUID, Must, ClonePointer, StateOf, EqualPointer) and the refusal type are the runtime's; each effect destination takes the must_land and idempotent that its component declares in gen.Context.Destinations, and generation refuses a destination that leaves one out (ST-SUP-RC32-OC12); the Parent list of an entity holds each reference to an entity with a resource type, with the permission and the relation of its References (ST-DECL-EN02). A service that declares no command gets no file and an empty wiring, because every archetype holds the command and query components (ST-SUP-RC20-OC39). The State of a row gives a jsonb field as its JSON text (json.RawMessage), which the audit runtime decodes (ST-SUP-RP05-LC03). KeyListRead gives the Read statement of the lookup of an upsert by its natural key, with the columns of Scan (ST-SUP-RC20-OC13).

title: query/generator.go
description: The generator for the query component. From the declared queries, entities, tenancy, authorization and fill slots that the compiler gives it in gen.Context, it emits the query slot contract out/queries (the read-only value with no secret field, the loaded type and query.Entity of each entity a query reads, and per query its request, response, handle and fill types, its query.Query, its repositories and its refusal values) and the handler package out/queries/serve: one handler per get and list query through query.Serve with Routes to mount them, a get query's decision of its declared permission on the requested row before the fill (through out/queries/internal/decide when it is not the read permission, while the fill's repositories keep the read permission), and the bind and run of each stream query through query.RunStream, each bound to the query's one fill. It gives the compiler no wiring: on the runtime data path the compiler's runtime wiring makes the handlers, mounts their routes and gives main.go one route per get and list query. It refuses a query whose fill does not implement the query slot, a route that net/http refuses or that conflicts, and a declaration that the query runtime cannot serve. On the runtime data path it is the Go model provider of the entities it reads. Handle, Run, Serve, the sealed cursor and the audit of reads live in the runtime library (ST-SUP-RP11); the parts that it emits and that are the same for every declaration move into the runtime, as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 (ST-SUP-RP11-LC17). render.go holds the rendering. Since the runtime update of 2026-11-11: the handlers bind through query.BindHTTP and query.BindContext, read the limit with query.Limit, write the page with query.EncodePage and a get response with query.EncodeValue, and set the refusal lookup of query.HTTP to queries.Declared, which knows the declared query.Refusal values of each query by identity; the loads read with Row.Int32, Row.Float, Row.Bytes and Row.JSON of the runtime (ST-SUP-RP11-LC17, ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05). For a get or list query with a gRPC method it emits Serve<Query>RPC on query.ServeRPC, and for a stream query Serve<Query>Stream on query.ServeStream, each generic in the method's messages and with the fill, the decision, Next, Encode and the refusal lookup of the HTTP handler (ST-SUP-RP11-LC19); the compiler marks a stream query in gen.Context.QueryStreams from the proto files (ST-SUP-RC33-OC08), and a stream query gets no HTTP route. A service that declares no query gets no file and an empty wiring, because every archetype holds the command and query components (ST-SUP-RC20-OC39).

title: capability/capability.go
description: The generator code that the command and query generators share (ST-SUP-RC32, ST-SUP-RC33): the Go names of a declared name with the rule of the domain-probe generator, the table name of an entity on the runtime data path, the read-only value type of an entity with its stored columns and Go types, its Go model, and the import of a fill package. It renders no file.

title: domainprobe/generator.go
description: The generator for the domain-probe component. From the declared observations and emitters that the compiler gives it in gen.Context, it emits the enum types, one probe type for each command, query, worker, process method and slot binding with one typed method for each observation that names it, the constructor that a handle binds a probe with, the Bind function and context accessor of each slot binding, the test constructors on probe.Recorder and the catalog observations.json, so it owns every contract of the component. It refuses each declaration that the probe runtime would refuse. The emit function, the sinks, the queues and Recorder live in the runtime library (ST-SUP-RP12). The compiler gives it the observations of the declaration and its commands, queries, workers and slot bindings as emitters (compiler.declaredEmitters).

title: worker/generator.go
description: Not written yet. The generator for the worker component. It emits, from the declared workers, the worker slot contracts, one runner for each worker with its schedule, lease or outbox destination handler, the registration of each runner in the worker mode, and the shutdown of every runner, so it owns every contract of the component. The worker handle is the command handle of the runtime library (ST-SUP-RP10-LF06). Operator note: a consumer fill that always fails keeps its must-land message pending until its attempts are exhausted; the outbox then parks it with an alert (ST-SUP-RP01-LC12) and holds back the later messages of its key, and only a person's discard through Resolve (ST-SUP-RP01-LC13) clears it.

title: httpsdestination/generator.go
description: Not written yet. The generator for the https-destination component. It checks each declared destination, renders the bounded HTTPS client from the shared template (ST-SUP-RC10-G02), emits one outbox destination handler and optional status lookup for each destination with its credential loading, and emits the fake partner for tests, so it owns every contract of the component.

title: oidcauth/generator.go
description: The generator of oidc-auth and Configure, the sign-in settings that oidc-auth and rh-sso-auth share. RuntimeAuth reads the issuer, the audience, the accepted algorithms, the subject claim, the role claim, the header and the CA file of the declaration, refuses a service that is not on the runtime data path, and refuses what the runtime verifier would refuse at start: an issuer that is not an HTTPS URL or holds a user, a query or a fragment, no audience, an algorithm outside the allow list RS256 and ES256 or named twice, a subject claim other than sub or oid, an issuer that is not the same text after TrimSpace, a role claim that is not a dotted path, a header that is not an HTTP field name and a CA file that is not an absolute clean path. Generate emits no file: the compiler gives these settings to the runtime verifier, which finds the key set through the discovery document of the issuer (ST-SUP-RP13-LC21). cmd/stego registers it, since the registry ships oidc-auth at ga (ST-SUP-Q99).
